title: streaming: lifecycle controls for client cancel/disconnect and resume (stream robustness)
author: Asha Menon
description:
Motivation: We observed multiple customer incidents where long-lived streaming connections either produced duplicate tokens after client reconnect or stalled when the client canceled without an explicit close. This PR introduces lifecycle controls to make streams resilient to client cancel/disconnect, support graceful resume/reconnect, and enforce server-side idle/total timeouts to bound resource usage.

Summary: Single-PR implementation across the serving runtime, OpenAI-compat adapter, and SDK-facing surface to: 1) add an explicit client cancel signal that can be sent over the streaming channel and handled without leaking KV cache or inflight request state; 2) detect abrupt TCP/websocket disconnects and start a short grace period allowing reconnect/resume with session tokens; 3) implement reconnect/resume semantics (best-effort token-continuity) for clients that reattach within the grace window; 4) add server-side idle and hard timeouts and metrics to prevent unbounded resource retention; 5) update OpenAI compatibility layer to expose cancel and resume semantics through the same streaming endpoints.

Design notes: - StreamingManager (runtime/streaming_manager.py) gains a lightweight per-stream lifecycle state machine: OPEN -> CANCELLING -> GRACE -> CLOSED. Cancel transitions allow the runtime to quickly stop generation but preserve enough KV cache and stream cursor state for a short GRACE window. If a client reconnects with the same session-id within the window, we attempt to rehydrate state and resume token emission. - For abrupt disconnects (socket close), the network layer emits a DISCONNECT event and we enter GRACE with a default 15s reconnect window (configurable). - A hard timeout (default 120s total) is enforced; exceeding it moves to CLOSED and frees resources. - The OpenAI-compat adapter adds two control frames: a control event with type=client_cancel and type=resume_attempt; these are optional and backward-compatible: older clients will still get the stream close event and behavior is unchanged. - SDKs: the TS/Python SDKs will be updated in follow-ups to expose the cancel API; for compatibility we expose a header (X-Redwood-Session) that lib callers can include for resume flows.

API/compat behavior: - Streaming endpoints accept query param session_id or X-Redwood-Session header. - To cancel: send control frame {"type":"client_cancel"} on the stream (OpenAI-compat SSE/HTTP streaming or websocket). The server responds with a terminal control frame and transitions to CANCELLING then GRACE. - To resume: re-open the stream with the same session_id and send {"type":"resume_attempt","cursor":<last_received_token_index>}. Resume is best-effort (may skip missing tokens on model-side recompute), so callers should deduplicate tokens if exact semantically-unique tokens are required.

Testing: - Unit tests for lifecycle transitions and timeouts (tests/test_streaming_lifecycle.py). - Integration tests that simulate client cancel, abrupt socket close, and reconnect within/outside grace window. - Added a flaky regression guard in CI that tests for duplicate token emission on reconnect.

Observability & rollout: - New metrics: streaming.session_started, streaming.session_cancelled, streaming.session_resumed, streaming.session_grace_expired, streaming.session_forced_closed, streaming.session_peak_memory. - Alerts: grace_expiry_rate > 1% for 10m triggers investigation; resume_success_rate < 95% triggers postmortem. - Rollout plan: feature gate behind runtime flag default-on for internal canary; monitor canary for 48h, then gradual rollout to production.

Backward compatibility: No breaking API changes. Control frames are optional; existing clients continue to function. For customers relying on older resume semantics (none), behavior remains as before (close on disconnect).

References: Linear ENG-2145 (stream resume), ENG-2190 (streaming timeouts), incident INT-889.

review_comments: Daniel Park (request changes): Can we make the grace window configurable per-customer? Concerned about long-tail resource retention for large fleets.
Author reply (Asha): Grace window is configurable via runtime config 'streaming.reconnect_grace_ms' and can be overridden per-tenant via Dedicated config. Added docs to streaming.md.
Maya Chen (nit): Please add more unit coverage around race between client_cancel and socket disconnect. Added tests and flakiness guard.

release_notes: Improved streaming robustness: client-triggered cancel, reconnect & resume within a grace window.
New server-side streaming timeouts to bound resource usage.
OpenAI compatibility: optional control frames for cancel/resume and X-Redwood-Session header for session resumption.
